record.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts:5-7 + addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 — server input contract is weaker than the client's and duplicates are persisted: the server schema lacks the uniqueness refinement the dialog has, and uniqueGuests only de-dupes against existing attendees (case-sensitively), never within the input array; a direct API call with ['a@x.com', 'a@x.com'] passes validation and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows (no unique constraint on (bookingId, email)), producing duplicate emails and duplicate ATTENDEE lines in the ICS.

adjudication.rationale: The client dialog validates guest emails with a uniqueness refinement (AddGuestsDialog.tsx: ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(...).refine(...)), but the server input schema only enforces `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness check (addGuests.schema.ts). In the handler, `uniqueGuests` filters only against existing booking attendees and a blacklist, but does not dedupe within the incoming `guests` array (and comparisons are case-sensitive) (addGuests.handler.ts: `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)`). Therefore an API call providing duplicate emails like ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] will pass server validation and produce duplicate entries in `guestsFullDetails`, which are then inserted via `attendees.createMany` without any `skipDuplicates` handling (addGuests.handler.ts). This can lead to duplicated attendee rows and downstream duplicated attendee data in calendar/email payloads.
